findings.issue_text: CryptoProvider.order() is added as an abstract interface method, breaking third-party CryptoProvider implementations; should be a default method for SPI backward compatibility

CryptoIntegration highest-order-wins provider selection ties at order 200 between DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider and WildFlyElytronProvider, so ServiceLoader classpath order silently decides and a misconfigured FIPS deployment can pick the non-FIPS provider instead of failing fast
CryptoIntegration logger.debugf(builder.toString()) passes the built message as the format string and the message ends with a dangling ', '; should use a format string with a joined list

AuthzClientCryptoProvider.concatenatedRSToASN1DER never checks signature.length >= signLength, so truncated input throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException from System.arraycopy instead of the declared IOException

ASN1Decoder.readInteger passes zero or -1 (indefinite) length straight to read()/new BigInteger, producing NegativeArraySizeException/NumberFormatException on malformed DER instead of IOException; should validate length > 0

AuthzClientCryptoProvider.integerToBytes silently truncates leading bytes whenever bytes.length > qLength, mangling oversized R or S values instead of rejecting them; should verify dropped bytes are exactly one zero byte

AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the JDK default KeyStore provider (typically SUN) rather than BouncyCastle, causing confusing NoSuchAlgorithmException for callers expecting BC-specific algorithms; should return null or document the substitute
AuthzClientCryptoProvider has two ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls whose results are discarded, causing dead allocations on every signature conversion

ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates the key pair once with default P-256 curve and reuses it for ES384/ES512, so those tests never exercise real 48/66-byte R/S integers or long-form DER lengths; keys should be generated per curve
ECDSAAlgorithmTest lacks negative tests for malformed DER, wrong sequence arity, truncated concatenated input, or high-bit R/S requiring a sign byte

CryptoIntegration.init is only wired into AuthzClient.create(Configuration), so other construction paths reaching new AuthzClient(Configuration) still fail with 'no crypto provider' at first signature use; consider moving the call into the constructor

per_golden_matches.reasoning: Both comments flag improper handling of an indefinite-length marker (-1). Despite different symptoms/locations, they point to the same underlying issue: -1/indefinite length must be validated/handled rather than treated as a normal length.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration highest-order-wins provider selection ties at order 200 between DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider and WildFlyElytronProvider, so ServiceLoader classpath order silently decides and a misconfigured FIPS deployment can pick the non-FIPS provider instead of failing fast
CryptoIntegration logger.debugf(builder.toString()) passes the built message as the format string and the message ends with a dangling ', '; should use a format string with a joined list

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` builds a message like `"Ignored crypto providers: " + <class names> + ", "` and calls `logger.debugf(builder.toString());`. Passing a prebuilt string to `debugf` as the format string is not a verifiable defect here because Java class names cannot contain `%` (so there are no format specifiers to misinterpret), and the trailing ", " is only cosmetic output, not a correctness/security bug. A reviewer might prefer `debug` or joining for cleaner output, but that's a style/nit rather than a real problem introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.concatenatedRSToASN1DER never checks signature.length >= signLength, so truncated input throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException from System.arraycopy instead of the declared IOException

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER(byte[] signature, int signLength), the code computes len = signLength/2 and then does System.arraycopy(signature, 0, r, 1, len) and System.arraycopy(signature, len, s, 1, len) without validating signature.length >= signLength. If the caller passes a shorter/truncated signature array, System.arraycopy will throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException (an unchecked runtime exception) rather than the declared/expected IOException handling in this method signature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readInteger passes zero or -1 (indefinite) length straight to read()/new BigInteger, producing NegativeArraySizeException/NumberFormatException on malformed DER instead of IOException; should validate length > 0
matched_golden_ids: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag improper handling of an indefinite-length marker (-1). The golden focuses on subsequent arithmetic using -1 leading to incorrect processing, while the candidate focuses on propagating -1 into reads/BigInteger causing runtime exceptions. Despite different symptoms/locations, they point to the same underlying issue: -1/indefinite length must be validated/handled rather than treated as a normal length.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.integerToBytes silently truncates leading bytes whenever bytes.length > qLength, mangling oversized R or S values instead of rejecting them; should verify dropped bytes are exactly one zero byte

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.integerToBytes, when s.toByteArray() returns more than qLength bytes, the method unconditionally drops the most-significant bytes (`System.arraycopy(bytes, bytes.length - tmp.length, ...)`) with no validation. For ECDSA R/S values parsed from ASN.1 DER, the only legitimate “extra” leading byte is a single 0x00 used to keep the INTEGER positive (minimal two’s complement encoding). As written, a malformed/oversized INTEGER (e.g., length > qLength+1, or length==qLength+1 with a non-zero leading byte) will be silently truncated to a different value rather than rejected, which is a verifiable correctness defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ECDSAAlgorithmTest generates the key pair once with default P-256 curve and reuses it for ES384/ES512, so those tests never exercise real 48/66-byte R/S integers or long-form DER lengths; keys should be generated per curve

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` creates a single `KeyPair` in the constructor via `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` without initializing a curve, and then reuses that same key for ES256/ES384/ES512. That means the ES384/ES512 cases are not guaranteed to use P-384/P-521 keys (and commonly will use the provider default, often P-256), so the test can pass by zero-padding in `integerToBytes(..., len)` when `algorithm.getSignatureLength()` is 96/132 even if the underlying signature r/s values are shorter. As a result, the ES384/ES512 tests may not actually exercise 48/66-byte r/s values or DER encodings representative of those curves, making the tests less meaningful for those algorithms.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ECDSAAlgorithmTest lacks negative tests for malformed DER, wrong sequence arity, truncated concatenated input, or high-bit R/S requiring a sign byte

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds ECDSAAlgorithmTest which performs a round-trip conversion check (DER -> concatenated RS -> DER -> concatenated RS) for ES256/384/512. The proposed finding is about missing additional negative/edge-case test coverage (malformed DER, wrong arity, truncation, high-bit sign-byte cases). While true as a testing suggestion, it does not identify a concrete bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced in the diff that can be verified from the changes; it’s a coverage enhancement request rather than a real problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.init is only wired into AuthzClient.create(Configuration), so other construction paths reaching new AuthzClient(Configuration) still fail with 'no crypto provider' at first signature use; consider moving the call into the constructor

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` added inside `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` and `create(InputStream)` delegates to `create(Configuration)`, so the documented public factory entry points shown in the diff are covered. The finding’s claim about “other construction paths reaching `new AuthzClient(Configuration)`” is not verifiable from the diff: no other `new AuthzClient(...)` call sites or an exposed constructor are shown, so asserting a failure path is speculative based on code not present in the diff.
